6.title: DNS Loopback on custom zones.
6.result: Access to the internal server by its domain name should succeed. The dns server resolves the domain name to the servers public IP address.

4.steps:
Scenario 1:
  1.	Locate the server on the lan subnet, create two address objects ftp_private and ftp_public for the servers private and public address on the Network->Address Objects page;
  2.	Set up a dns server A on the wan side, create an entry with domain name ftp.test.com resolved to the servers public ip address;
  3.	On the NAT policies page, add a custom policy as below:
  Original source: lan subnets
  Translated source:wan interface ip
  Original destination:ftp_public
  Translated destination:ftp_private
  Original service:ftp
  Translated service:original
  Inbound interface:Any
  Outbound interface:Any
  Click the ok button after completed;
  4.	On the firewall, Add an allow access rule from wan->lan with destination ftp_public for ftp service of all users;
  5.	From another host on the lan( set A as its dns server), try to access the ftp server: ftp://ftp.test.com
  6.	Test above steps for http, ping, smtp, pop3,telnet service etc.
  Scenario 2:
  If you do not have a dns server, you can test this feature with DDNS.
  1.	Configure the DDNS settings correctly on the Network->DDNS page, make sure that the domain name you filled can be resolved to the wan interface ip, for example, rosa001.ddns.ms resolved to 10.103.16.240;
  2.	Add a custom policy as below:
  Original source: lan subnets
  Translated source:wan interface ip
  Original destination:wan interface ip
  Translated destination:ftp_private
  Original service:ftp
  Translated service:original
  Inbound interface:Any
  Outbound interface:Any
  Click the ok button after completed;
  3.	From a host on the lan, try to access the ftp server by ftp://rosa001.ddns.ms.
  4.	Test for different services like http, telnet, smtp etc.
